standard_prerequisites.name: Pushout of a span
standard_prerequisites.statement: Y sqcup^X Z is generated by inl : Y -> ..., inr : Z -> ... and glue : prd x:X inl(j x) = inr(k x).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the base of the fibration E constructed in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flattening lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a family P over a coequalizer defined recursively by a family C and a family of equivalences D, the total space Sigma P is equivalent to the flattened higher inductive type.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied at source line 1273 with the explicit values listed afterwards.

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: An equivalence between types gives a path between them by ua.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes map E (glue x) = ua(e_X(x)) a well-typed clause of the recursive definition.

core_obligations: Define E : Y sqcup^X Z -> type by the recursion principle of the pushout, with E(inl y) := E_Y(y), E(inr z) := E_Z(z) and map E (glue x) := ua(e_X(x)) (source lines 1262-1270).
Apply the flattening lemma with A := Y + Z, B := X, f(x) := inl(j x), g(x) := inr(k x), C defined componentwise by E_Y and E_Z, and D := e_X (source lines 1273-1285).
Identify the base higher inductive type W of the flattening lemma with the pushout Y sqcup^X Z and the recursively defined family P with the E constructed above (source lines 1287-1289).

Read off from the flattening lemma that the total space Sigma E is equivalent to the flattened type with the displayed generators, which is the pushout square asserted in the statement (source lines 1291-1314).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the fibration by pushout recursion.
Instantiate the flattening lemma with the explicit A, B, f, g, C, D.
Translate the flattened type back into the pushout square for the total space.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 8.5.3 at source lines 1235-1259: given fibrations E_Y over Y and E_Z over Z together with an equivalence e_X between their pullbacks along j and k, there is a fibration E over the pushout restricting to E_Y and E_Z with map E (glue x) = ua(e_X(x)), and its total space fits in the displayed pushout square. The author's proof (source lines 1261-1314) is a two-stage construction: the fibration is first defined by the recursion principle of the pushout, which requires the univalence clause and the two definitional clauses (lines 1262-1270), and the pushout square for the total space is then obtained by instantiating the flattening lemma with four explicitly listed pieces of data, namely the type A = Y + Z, the maps f and g built from j and k, the family C defined componentwise by E_Y and E_Z, and the family of equivalences D := e_X (lines 1273-1285). Only after identifying the flattening lemma's base type with the pushout and its family with E does the conclusion follow (lines 1287-1314). The statement records none of this data.
